private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that preserves a meaningful margin. Use subsequent published rates and allocated hours to estimate price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $325 rate was below both competitors’ $350 rates and yielded 821 hours and approximately $102,619 in profit. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how sensitive our allocation is to price.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly while remaining below both competitors. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned approximately $74,690. The other firms charged $325 and $350, so there is not yet enough information to estimate how a rate change affects our hours.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate increase to assess the margin–volume tradeoff without making a large change to our competitive position. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $350 rate generated 498 allocated hours and approximately $74,690 profit. Competitors charged $325 and $350; one quarter is insufficient to estimate how allocation responds to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate increase while preserving a competitive position. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1, accounting for changes in competitors' published rates, before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Q2's $15 rate increase coincided with 45 fewer allocated hours but about $6,000 more profit. Both competitors also raised their rates; our $340 rate remained the lowest.
private_notes.plan: Increase modestly to $355, staying below both competitors' latest published rates. Reassess allocated hours and profit next quarter, especially if competitors change their pricing.

private_notes.observations: Q2 profit rose to about $83,200 from $74,700 in Q1 despite our rate increasing from $350 to $360; allocated hours rose from 498 to 520. Competitor rates also increased, so this does not isolate the effect of our price change.
private_notes.plan: Increase our rate moderately to $375. Track allocated hours and profit next quarter to assess whether the additional margin outweighs any volume loss; avoid drawing strong conclusions from two quarters of data.

private_notes.observations: Q2 profit rose despite hours falling from 498 to 471 as our rate increased from $350 to $365. Competitors also raised rates; our premium over the lowest-priced firm remained $25.
private_notes.plan: Continue a measured increase while monitoring whether lost hours begin to outweigh the higher margin. Avoid a sharp increase that could shift substantial work to competitors or in-house.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose each quarter despite modest declines in allocated hours as our rate increased. Our Q3 rate of $355 remained below both competitors’ published rates of $375 and $380.
private_notes.plan: Increase to $370, maintaining a discount to both competitors’ latest published rates. Reassess hours and profit after Q4 before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose from about $83,204 in Q2 to $87,430 in Q3 despite allocated hours falling from 520 to 500. Both other firms also raised their rates by $15 in Q3. Three quarters are insufficient to estimate how strongly allocation responds to price.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate moderately to $390, preserving our recent position relative to the other firms if their increases continue. Monitor hours and profit before considering a larger change.

private_notes.observations: Rates rose $15 each quarter while allocated hours declined from 498 to 452; quarterly profit nevertheless increased from $74,690 to $81,370. Competitors have also raised rates steadily.
private_notes.plan: Continue the measured $15 increase. Monitor whether declining hours or competitors' rates begin to offset the higher margin.

private_notes.observations: Profit increased in each of Q1–Q4 despite successive $15 rate increases, while allocated hours declined from 821 to 708. Both other panel firms also raised rates each quarter and remained above ours.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate by $15 to $385, preserving the established pricing approach without risking a sharp loss of hours. Review Q5 allocation and the next published rate card before considering a larger increase.

private_notes.observations: Rates rose across the panel through Q4. Our quarterly profit increased despite hours falling from 520 in Q2 to 474 in Q4; at $390, our rate remained $20 above Arden & Cole and $5 below Calder Rowe.
private_notes.plan: Increase moderately to $405, maintaining our recent position if competitors continue raising rates by roughly $15. Monitor the resulting hours and profit before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Rates rose by $15 each quarter across the panel. Our allocated hours declined from 498 to 429, while reported quarterly profit rose from $74,690 to $83,714.
private_notes.plan: Set $410, continuing the measured increase. Reassess if the loss of hours begins to outweigh the higher margin; make future decisions independently of competitors' pricing patterns.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose each quarter through Q5 despite declining hours. Our rate remained $20–$25 below the other panel firms in Q5, and their rates have generally risen by $15 per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Increase moderately to $410. This captures more margin while remaining below competitors’ most recently published rates. Reassess the hours response and new panel rates next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have each raised rates by $15 in the last three quarters. Keeping our rate $20 above Arden and $5 below Calder has produced rising profit, though the latest increase was small as allocated hours declined.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate by $15 to maintain our recent position if competitors continue their pattern. Reassess next quarter using the resulting hours and profit.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose through Q5, but the latest $15 rate increase added only $703 in profit while allocated hours fell by 27. Competitor rates also rose, so the history does not isolate the effect of our rate.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $420. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q5 before making another increase; avoid assuming competitors will continue raising rates.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose through Q5 at $385, then fell in Q6 when our rate increased to $410 and allocated hours dropped from 663 to 518. Our discount to the other panel firms also narrowed substantially.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate to restore a meaningful price advantage and recover hours. Monitor whether the resulting profit exceeds Q5’s $122,611 before raising rates again.

private_notes.observations: Quarterly profit has risen as our rate increased from $350 to $420, despite allocated hours declining from 498 to 424. The other panel firms have also raised their rates; in Q6 Arden & Cole charged $410 and Calder Rowe charged $420.
private_notes.plan: Set $435, continuing a measured increase. Next quarter, assess whether the additional margin offsets any loss of hours, and adjust based on observed demand rather than assuming competitors will continue raising rates.

private_notes.observations: Profit increased in Q6 despite a $10 rate increase, as allocated hours rose to 424 while the other panel firms also raised rates. The allocation formula and future competing rates remain uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Set $435 for Q7, a measured increase. Compare realized hours and profit against Q6 before considering further changes; do not assume other firms will continue raising rates.

private_notes.observations: The $395 rate in Q7 produced 713 hours and $139,112 profit, exceeding Q5’s $122,611. A $40 discount to both other firms coincided with substantially more hours than the $10 discount in Q6.
private_notes.plan: Hold the $395 rate for Q8 to preserve the price advantage and test whether it continues to generate strong profit. Reassess after seeing Q8 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $435 in Q7, allocated hours fell to 321 and profit fell to $75,329, versus 424 hours and $93,354 at $420 in Q6. Arden & Cole lowered its rate to $395 in Q7, widening our price gap.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate to regain hours while retaining a substantial margin over the $200 hourly cost. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $435 in Q7, allocated hours fell to 321 and profit to $75,329, down from 424 hours and $93,354 at $420 in Q6. Arden & Cole also cut its rate from $410 to $395, so the decline cannot be attributed solely to our increase.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the Q8 rate to $415 to improve competitiveness while retaining a substantial margin. Compare Q8 hours and profit with Q6 and Q7 before making another change.

private_notes.observations: At $395, allocated hours fell from 713 in Q7 to 603 in Q8 as competitors reduced their rates. Q8 profit was $117,612, below Q5's $122,611 at a $385 rate with competitors at $405 and $410.
private_notes.plan: Set $385 to regain a stronger price advantage while retaining a substantial margin over the $200 hourly cost. Reassess using Q9 hours and the published rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q8’s $410 rate restored hours to 447 and produced $93,832 in profit, the highest quarterly profit so far. At $435 in Q7, hours fell sharply; the evidence for raising the rate again is weak.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $410 to preserve the recovered workload and a strong margin. Reassess after the next allocation and published rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q8's $415 rate produced 404 hours and $86,924 in profit, recovering from Q7's $435 rate and 321 hours. Q6 earned $93,354 at $420, but competing rates were higher then, so its result is not directly comparable.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $415 for Q9. This preserves the Q8 improvement without a further rate increase that could reduce hours. Reassess after seeing Q9 allocations and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $385 in Q9, we received 691 hours and earned $127,755, with competitors at $410 and $415. At $395 against those same competitor rates in Q8, we received only 603 hours. Our strongest quarterly profit came when our rate was $40 below both competitors.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to seek more hours while preserving a $175 margin per hour. Reassess after Q10, particularly if competitors change their rates.

private_notes.observations: At $410, allocated hours fell from 447 in Q8 to 419 in Q9 as Arden lowered its rate to $385. Q7's $435 rate produced substantially lower profit. The strongest recent quarterly profits were around $93,000 at rates of $410–$420 when competitors were priced closer.
private_notes.plan: Set $400 to narrow the gap with Arden and seek enough additional hours to offset the $10 lower margin per hour. Reassess using the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $415, allocated hours fell from 404 in Q8 to 379 in Q9 as Arden & Cole lowered its rate from $395 to $385. Our Q9 profit was $81,483, below Q8's $86,924.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to $410, matching Birchwood Hale's latest published rate while preserving a strong margin. Assess whether the change recovers enough hours to improve profit before making further adjustments.

private_notes.plan: Set $400 to improve competitiveness while retaining a $200-per-hour margin. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q10 before adjusting again.

private_notes.plan: Maintain $375 this quarter to protect allocated hours while retaining a strong margin. Reassess using subsequent allocation and published rate-card data.

private_notes.observations: Q11 earned $90,666 at $395 with 465 hours. Higher rates have sometimes earned more, but Q7’s $435 rate caused a sharp drop in hours. Recent panel rates have declined.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $395. Preserve the current volume and margin balance, then reassess when Q12 hours and the new rate card are available.

private_notes.observations: Q11’s $400 rate produced 421 hours and approximately $84,142 in profit, improving on Q10’s $410 rate and 367 hours. Competitor rates remained at $375 and $395 in Q11.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to $395 to test whether additional hours outweigh the $5 reduction in hourly margin. Reassess after observing the allocation and next rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $375, Arden & Cole earned $118,758 in Q12 with 679 allocated hours. Both competing firms posted $395 rates. Recent allocations have softened, but the data do not establish that changing our rate would improve profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $375 to preserve a $175 hourly margin and a competitive rate advantage. Reassess after observing next quarter’s allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $395, Q11–Q12 delivered 465 and 455 hours, yielding about $90.7k and $88.7k. Earlier, $390 with a similar panel rate card delivered 474 hours and about $90.1k profit. Arden remains at $375 and Calder has fallen to $395.
private_notes.plan: Reduce modestly to $390 to seek more hours without materially sacrificing margin. Reassess after observing Q13 allocation and the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $395 in Q12, Calder Rowe received 455 hours and earned $88,704, an improvement over Q11's 421 hours and $84,142 at $400. Allocation varies across quarters, so the effect of the $5 reduction is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a further modest reduction to $390. It needs roughly 12 additional hours versus Q12 to offset the lower margin. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $375, allocated hours fell from 738 in Q10 to 648 in Q13 as competitors’ rates declined toward $390. Q13 profit was approximately $113,336.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to improve competitiveness and seek more hours while retaining a $170 margin per hour. Reassess after the next allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $390 in Q13, we received 480 hours and earned about $91,158, up from 455 hours and $88,704 at $395 in Q12. Competitor rates were unchanged across those quarters.
private_notes.plan: Test a further $5 reduction. At $385, approximately 493 hours would match Q13 profit; evaluate the resulting allocation and next rate card before making another change.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $370 to preserve a competitive rate while avoiding another reduction in margin. Reassess after seeing Q15 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q14's cut to $385 increased hours to 489 but reduced profit to $90,450 from Q13's $91,158. Competitors also cut rates by $5, so the result does not isolate the effect of our rate change. Large premiums have previously caused substantial hour losses.

private_notes.observations: The Q14 reduction to $385 increased hours from 480 to 489, but profit fell from $91,158 to $90,450. Both competitors also reduced their rates by $5. A further $5 cut would need roughly 14 additional hours to improve on Q14 profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $385 rather than continue cutting into margin. Review the next allocation and rate card for evidence that a different rate would improve long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: Rival rates have declined for four consecutive quarters, and our hours fell from 660 to 643 despite holding our rate at $370. Recent quarterly profits have also declined.
private_notes.plan: Set $365 to maintain a modest price advantage as competitors lower their rates. Reassess the margin-versus-hours tradeoff after Q16.

private_notes.observations: At $380 in Q15, we received 527 hours and earned $94,823—our highest quarterly profit in the history shown. The other firms' rates were $370 and $385.

private_notes.observations: At $385, profit was about $90,450 in Q14 and $88,182 in Q15. Birchwood lowered its rate from $385 to $380 in Q15, while our allocated hours fell from 489 to 477. Recent results do not establish that raising our rate would improve profit.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $365 to preserve a modest price advantage without sacrificing more margin. Reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $380, the last two quarters produced 527 and 510 hours and about $94,823 and $91,719 in profit. Recent higher rates have not reliably improved profit. Arden & Cole has lowered its rate to $365; Calder Rowe remains at $385.

private_notes.observations: At $385, allocated hours fell from 489 in Q14 to 461 in Q16 as competing rates declined. Quarterly profit fell from $90,450 to $85,296.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to $380 to improve competitiveness against Birchwood while retaining a substantial margin. Reassess after observing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.plan: Hold $365 to retain a modest price advantage. Reassess if competitors cut rates or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $380, the last three quarters yielded 527, 510, and 497 hours, with profits of about $94,800, $91,700, and $89,500. Nearby historical rates have not consistently produced higher profit.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $380 rate. The recent decline in hours warrants monitoring, but the evidence does not yet justify reducing the margin to chase additional work. Reassess after the next allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $380 in Q17, we received 497 hours and earned $89,548. Competitors charged $365 and $380. Recent allocations have generally improved as our rate fell, though profits have remained near $90,000.

private_notes.plan: Hold $365 to preserve our price advantage without accelerating the panel’s rate declines. Reassess if competitors cut further or our allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.plan: Test $375 for one quarter to see whether a modest rate reduction restores enough hours to offset the lower margin. Reassess using the resulting hours and profit.

private_notes.observations: At $375 in Q18, we received 536 hours and earned $93,764, the highest profit in the displayed 12 quarters. Competing rates were $365 and $380. The $5 reduction from Q17 coincided with 39 more hours, though allocation can fluctuate independently of price.
private_notes.plan: Test a further $5 reduction to $370. It needs roughly 16 additional hours versus Q18 to improve quarterly profit. Reassess the allocation and competitors’ rates next quarter rather than assuming the Q18 increase was entirely price-driven.

private_notes.observations: At $365, allocated hours fell from 688 in Q16 to 621 in Q19 as competitors cut their rates to $375 and $370. Q19 profit was $102,480. We retain a modest price advantage, but further cuts could accelerate the panel’s downward rate trend.

private_notes.observations: At $375 in Q19, we received 509 hours and earned $88,988, up from 485 hours and $87,265 at $380 in Q18. Rival rates have continued to decline, and quarterly hours fluctuate, so one quarter does not establish that another cut would improve profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold $375 for another quarter to assess whether the volume gain persists. Reconsider the rate using subsequent hours and profit rather than pursuing cuts based on a single observation.

private_notes.observations: At $370 in Q19, we received 562 hours and earned approximately $95,537, our highest quarterly profit in the displayed history. Arden held at $365, while Birchwood reduced its rate to $375. Recent $5 reductions in our rate have generally coincided with enough additional hours to offset the lower margin, although allocation varies for other reasons.
private_notes.plan: Test $365, matching Arden. Compared with Q19, this requires roughly 18 additional hours to improve quarterly profit. Review the resulting hours and next rate card before making another change; avoid assuming every allocation change is caused by our rate.
